matchstick.title: Check arithmetic validity
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, compute the numeric values of both sides of the equation and verify that the equality holds; without this, the solver may accept an invalid equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Always, after proposing a stick move and before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Accepting a transformed equation without confirming that the left and right sides evaluate to the same number.

matchstick.title: Preserve valid numeral shapes
matchstick.principle: When a stick is removed from or added to a Roman numeral, the resulting glyph must correspond to a valid Roman numeral (or be removed entirely if it becomes empty); without this, the solver may produce an invalid numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a stick is moved to or from a numeral character.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from V and leaving a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Operator integrity: stick composition and validity
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick involving an operator, ensure the operator’s stick count and orientation remain those of a valid operator (+, -, =); without this, the operator may become an illegal symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a stick is moved from or to an operator character.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from '+' without converting it to '-', leaving an invalid '+' missing its vertical component.

matchstick.title: Match‑stick orientation matters
matchstick.principle: A stick’s orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) is fixed; you cannot replace a vertical stick with a diagonal or rotate it; without this, the solver may create impossible shapes.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During any stick relocation, respect the original orientation of the moved stick.
matchstick.example: Changing a diagonal stick from V into a vertical stick to form I.

matchstick.title: Limit changes to two characters
matchstick.principle: A single stick move can affect only the source character (which loses a stick) and the destination character (which gains a stick); without this, the solver may inadvertently modify more than two characters.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When planning a stick move, ensure only two characters change.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from one numeral and also adding a new stick elsewhere without removing it from anywhere, effectively adding a stick.

matchstick.title: Maintain a valid equality
matchstick.principle: The final equation must contain exactly one '=' sign, which must remain the standard two‑horizontal‑stick form; without this, the equation may lose its equality sign or become malformed.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any stick move, verify that the '=' sign is unchanged and still consists of two horizontal sticks.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal stick from '=' and not replacing it, turning it into a single '-' sign.

matchstick.title: Transform numerals via single stick moves
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick between numerals, consider known single‑stick transformations (e.g., I↔II, V↔X) to keep both source and destination as valid numerals; without this, the move may produce invalid numerals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When evaluating possible stick moves between numeral characters.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from V to I and ending up with an invalid shape for both symbols.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: Provide the corrected equation as a single line prefixed with 'Correct version of the equation: ', with uppercase and whitespace collapsed; without this, the answer may not be parsed correctly.
matchstick.example: Omitting the required prefix or using a different case, causing the verifier to miss the answer.

matchstick.title: Plus-to-minus conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If the equation contains a '+' operator, consider moving its vertical stick to a numeral (or to the left side) to turn '+' into '-' and adjust numeric values; without this, the solver may miss a common valid transformation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation includes a '+' and the arithmetic does not balance, try moving the vertical stick from '+' to a numeral.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from '+' to a numeral but leaving '+' unchanged, resulting in an invalid '+' missing its vertical component.

matchstick.title: Advanced numeral transformations: diagonal swaps and numeral deletion
matchstick.principle: When moving sticks between numerals, consider swapping components (e.g., moving a diagonal from V to I to turn VI into IV) or deleting a single‑stick numeral (e.g., moving the I from VI to another numeral, leaving V); ensure the resulting numerals are valid; without this, the solver may overlook viable solutions.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When V and I appear adjacent or when a single‑stick numeral can be removed to balance the equation.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from V to I but leaving V as a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on making a syntactically valid transformation and forgets to check whether the resulting equation is numerically true.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the numeric values of both sides after a proposed stick move and confirm the equality before finalizing the answer.

matchstick.why_it_happens: When moving a stick, the model may produce a glyph that does not correspond to any Roman numeral, often by removing a necessary stick or adding a stick of the wrong orientation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Apply the 'Preserve valid numeral shapes' principle and check that each altered numeral matches a known Roman numeral pattern.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may add or remove sticks from an operator without respecting the exact stick count and orientation required for '+', '-', or '=', creating an illegal operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Use the 'Operator integrity' principle to ensure any operator after a stick move still matches the defined composition of a valid operator.

matchstick.description: Missing destination for moved stick (effectively removing a stick)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes removes a stick from a character without placing it elsewhere, violating the rule that exactly one stick must be relocated.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When selecting a source stick, always identify a valid destination character and apply the move to both source and destination.

matchstick.why_it_happens: After moving a stick from an operator, the remaining sticks may no longer form a recognized operator, e.g., turning '+' into a lone vertical line.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Apply the 'Operator integrity' principle: after moving a stick, verify that the operator still matches one of the allowed symbols (+, -, =).
